hero.headline: Vero Beach parents sue city over infant son's remains allegedly disturbed, reburied without consent
hero.teaser: Two Vero Beach parents have filed an amended lawsuit against the City of Vero Beach, alleging their infant son's remains were accidentally disturbed during maintenance at Crestlawn Cemetery and then reinterred without their knowledge or consent.
hero.body:
Adam Chrzan and Tanya Crovo's son, identified only as A.C., died in August 2007 at 37 days old. According to the complaint, he was buried at Crestlawn Cemetery on Aug. 15, 2007, where his parents believed he had remained undisturbed for nearly 18 years. The parents allege that sometime between the burial in 2007 and April 2025, maintenance or irrigation work was taking place near the burial site when heavy equipment breached the grave. The lawsuit centers on Crestlawn Cemetery, which is operated by the City of Vero Beach.

The lawsuit alleges A.C.'s casket, contents, and remains were damaged or destroyed. According to the complaint, someone acting in an official capacity for the City of Vero Beach then directed cemetery workers to collect the remains, place them into a new casket and reinter the child without notifying or obtaining consent from the parents. The lawsuit claims the parents were deprived of the opportunity to participate in laying their son to rest again and were never informed that the burial site had allegedly been disturbed. The parents say they did not learn what allegedly happened until April 2025. The lawsuit does not explain how they became aware of the alleged disturbance, but an attorney for the family said that information could come out during the legal proceedings.

The amended complaint accuses the city and cemetery of tortious interference with a burial plot and human remains, negligence, negligent infliction of emotional distress, intentional misrepresentation, and fraudulent concealment. The lawsuit also alleges the city failed to protect the burial site and failed to follow Florida laws and administrative rules governing cemetery maintenance, disinterment and the handling of human remains. "The Defendant's conduct is outrageous and goes beyond all bounds of decency in a civilized society, is not dignified and is intolerable," the complaint states. This amended complaint comes after a judge dismissed the family's original lawsuit. The dismissal was not a finding that the allegations were false. Instead, the court ruled the legal claims, as originally pleaded, could not proceed against the city under Florida law.

The City of Vero Beach declined to comment on the newly filed amended complaint. In court filings responding to the original lawsuit, the city disputed the parents' allegation that irrigation work could have caused the damage. The city's attorney submitted a survey stating there are no irrigation lines adjacent to the burial plot of A.C. The filing says the closest sprinkler heads are approximately 10 feet north of the burial plot and about 40 feet south. The family's attorneys did not rule out the possibility of seeking to exhume the gravesite as part of the litigation. A judge has not yet ruled on the amended complaint.

cards.headline: Suspect identified in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher in St. Lucie County
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified the suspect in a shooting that killed a 66-year-old man on Tuesday. The fatal shooting happened at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. The victim was identified as Andre Leonard Barnes, 66, of Fort Pierce. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

The suspect in this homicide investigation has been identified as Dale A. Mincey. Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Schools, and the district released a statement following his death. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: Second decomposed body found near US-1 in Sebastian this week
cards.teaser: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, the second body discovered in the area this week.
cards.body: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, prompting a death investigation by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. A caller reported finding the body shortly after 4 p.m. The body was located on the east side of US 1, across the street from where the body of James Thompson was found Monday. Detectives and Crime Scene Unit personnel are processing the area and working to identify the deceased. Investigators are working to determine whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.

cards.headline: 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 moves forward in St. Lucie County despite neighbor opposition
cards.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality despite pushback from neighbors who say it will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August.

The proposed development is 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres. That area is equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches. Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. Lewis said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "We will be surrounded," said Lewis. "I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build." She added that her dogs and horses currently have 10 acres to run around on, but that will change with the development.

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," said Benton. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. Lewis said she is worried this development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," said Lewis. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like."

cards.headline: Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness holds fundraiser workout for family of 5-year-old killed in bike accident
cards.body:
A Jensen Beach Orangetheory Fitness is rallying its community to support the family of Garrett Leonard, a 5-year-old boy who was killed in an accident. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says Garrett was riding a bicycle in between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami when he was hit as he crossed the path of a pickup truck. The sheriff's office says the driver cooperated in the investigation and told reporters on Wednesday that no charges had been filed in the case.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier and gym owner Tabitha Lavery learned of the tragedy that struck two of their members and didn't hesitate to act. Collier said when she realized what happened it was gut wrenching and heart wrenching. Her first thought was that the gym always comes together as a community and that they had to do something. Lavery described the couple as valued members of the community and called them a great couple. Collier said that as a parent she cannot even imagine that type of pain and believes the only thing that can get you through something like that is being supported.

Collier reflected on the pride Garrett's father showed for his son, saying he would say "this is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad." Lavery said it was important to them that they help in any way they can. The two organized a fundraiser workout to support the family during this difficult time. Lavery explained that they put together a 90-minute fundraiser workout to help the family get through this hard time.

All of the proceeds from the workout will go toward a GoFundMe that was started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one. The workout is scheduled for this Sunday and is open to the public. Garrett's family was not ready to provide a statement on Wednesday but shared photos with the news station.

hero.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of inaugural August season
hero.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The New York Heights and the Boston Hunters round out the four-team league.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. Whitmore told The Associated Press at a scrimmage in March that this is just every little girl's dream to play professional baseball, and now for us to actually be with each other, there's so much freedom and peace within it. The league hopes to create a space for women's baseball players similar to the one the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League did 70 years ago.

Each team name holds unique meaning tied to pioneering women. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

The team logos reflect their unique identities. The Heights logo includes graphic lines surrounding a baseball, mimicking the speed of a fastball and resembling the New York skyline. The Firebells logo fuses a bell with a phoenix. The Queens logo is a capital Q topped with four baseball diamonds. The Hunters logo is an osprey clasping a baseball bat in its talons. The league, which has been years in the making, is now set to begin play with these four teams representing cities across the country.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi leads Argentina to 3-2 comeback over Egypt, reaches World Cup quarterfinals
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable 3-2 victory over Egypt on Tuesday despite trailing by two with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2 against Egypt on Tuesday. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete the comeback after Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Messi, who was in tears after the final whistle, also missed a chance in the first half when his penalty kick was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico.

Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said he was so emotional about what a group of players the team has. For much of the game, it looked like it would be a painful exit for the 39-year-old Messi in what might be the last of his six World Cups. Egypt took a surprising lead in the 15th minute when Ibrahim got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross. Despite being the all-time leading scorer at World Cups, Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at the tournament.

cards.headline: United States eliminated from World Cup in 4-1 loss to Belgium at home
cards.teaser: Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth and ended U.S. hopes for a deep World Cup run at home.
cards.body:
The United States' hopes for a deep World Cup run at home ended when Charles De Ketelaere scored twice and assisted on another goal, helping Belgium expose the Americans' defensive liabilities in a 4-1 win Monday night that earned a quarterfinal berth. While the U.S. was boosted by the presence of star forward Folarin Balogun, whose one-game red-card suspension was controversially lifted by FIFA, American defenders were at fault in a pair of first-half goals and goalkeeper Matt Freese's gaffe gave the Red Devils a third early in the second half. Second-half substitute Romelu Lukaku added Belgium's final goal in the third minute of stoppage time. Malik Tillman tied the score 1-1 midway through the first half with his second free kick goal of the tournament, but the Americans conceded just 61 seconds after the ensuing kickoff. U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino showed his frustration by kicking a rack in front of the bench, sending four water bottles flying.

American star Christian Pulisic could only watch from the bench after injuring his right foot when he hit a boot of Belgium captain Youri Tielemans on a 52nd-minute shot attempt. Pulisic favored his foot after that and was replaced seven minutes later. Seeking its first World Cup title, Belgium knocked the U.S. out in the round of 16 for the second time in 12 years and extended its unbeaten streak to 18 games. The Red Devils play 2010 champion Spain on Friday at Inglewood, California, for a semifinal berth against France or Morocco. After winning three games in a World Cup for the first time in this expanded 48-nation tournament, the U.S. failed in its quest to reach the quarterfinals for the first time since 2002 and lost to Belgium for the seventh straight time since a victory at the initial tournament in 1930. A crowd of 66,925 at Lumen Field watched the match.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup match draws biggest soccer audience in U.S. history with 30 million viewers
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported, drawing more than 30 million viewers.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match drew more than 30 million viewers, making it the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said its World Cup broadcasts have generated significant interest beyond U.S. matches. The network said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: IOC ends neutral status vetting for Russian athletes ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
cards.teaser: The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
cards.body:
The IOC advised Olympic sports bodies on Tuesday to end a three-year program vetting Russians for neutral status ahead of qualifying events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The move was expected since the International Olympic Committee advised two months ago that athletes from Belarus, Russia's military ally in the full military invasion of Ukraine, should be allowed again to compete with their full national identity. The IOC eased entry requirements to its own events for Russian athletes and teams while provisionally lifting its suspension since October 2023 of the Russian Olympic Committee. The terms of that suspension, imposed when the Russian Olympic body incorporated regional sports councils from occupied regions of Ukraine, no longer applied, the IOC said.

Just 32 athletes from Russia and Belarus competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics as approved neutrals and combined to win five medals. The Russian team had more than 300 athletes at the 2021 Tokyo Olympics and won 71 medals. The IOC did not yet approve letting Russian athletes and teams compete with their flag and anthem. That decision will come at an appropriate time, it said. The next Olympic competition is the 2026 Youth Summer Games in Dakar, Senegal opening Oct. 31. The IOC said to address the lack of confidence in the global sporting community relating to the return of Russian athletes to international competition, those athletes must give multiple doping controls and be part of a recognized testing program.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival is a recurring event in Indian River County that draws residents and visitors to celebrate local seafood and coastal culture. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the annual gathering.

The event has been held for 17 consecutive years in Vero Beach. Organizers announced the festival will take place in November 2026, continuing the tradition that has become a fixture in the local events calendar.

Further details about the specific dates, location, and vendors will be announced by the promoters in the coming months.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office says Garrett was riding a bicycle in between vehicles at a motocross park in Miami when he was hit as he crossed the path of a pickup truck. The sheriff's office says the driver cooperated in the investigation and told reporters on Wednesday that no charges had been filed in the case.

Orangetheory coach Shelby Collier and gym owner Tabitha Lavery learned of the tragedy that struck two of their members and didn't hesitate to act. Collier said when she realized what happened it was gut wrenching and heart wrenching. Her first thought was that the gym always comes together as a community and that they had to do something. Lavery described the couple as valued members of the community and called them a great couple. Collier said that as a parent she cannot even imagine that type of pain and believes the only thing that can get you through something like that is being supported.

Collier reflected on the pride Garrett's father showed for his son, saying he would say "this is Garrett, look what he did, look what he did, and just the proudest dad." Lavery said it was important to them that they help in any way they can. The two organized a fundraiser workout to support the family during this difficult time. Lavery explained that they put together a 90-minute fundraiser workout to help the family get through this hard time.

All of the proceeds from the workout will go toward a GoFundMe that was started to ease the financial burden that comes with losing a loved one. The workout is scheduled for this Sunday and is open to the public. Garrett's family was not ready to provide a statement on Wednesday but shared photos with the news station.

hero.headline: Neighbors push back on 85-acre Indrio Town Center development near I-95 in St. Lucie County
hero.teaser: A proposed 85-acre mixed-use development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road is moving closer to reality after county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace.
hero.body:
A proposed 85-acre development off Indrio Road and Russakis Road in St. Lucie County is moving closer to reality, but neighbors are pushing back against plans they say will transform the area's rural character. The project, called Indrio Town Center, would bring a mix of commercial and retail space and possibly residential units to land near Interstate 95. On June 18, county planning and zoning unanimously recommended rezoning the land from agricultural to planned retail workplace. County commissioners are expected to vote on the rezoning in August. The proposed development is 447,250 square feet of commercial, retail and possible residential space across more than 85 acres, an area equivalent to more than 48 FIFA-standard soccer pitches.

Susan Lewis has lived near the proposed site for 15 years, running a farm rescue on a property that has been in her family for decades. She said the development would surround her property and worsen existing conditions. "I have dogs that have 10 acres to run around. I have horses that have 10 acres to run around. It's gone," Lewis said. "We will be surrounded. I think that there's plenty of other places for them to build." Lewis said she is worried the development will change the rural landscape in St. Lucie County. "We moved here for a reason; this is why we do what we do," said Lewis. "We like to be in the wilderness. This is what Florida used to look like."

County Planning and Zoning Manager Kori Benton said the land is part of a planned design area called Town, Villages and Countryside, along with 14,000 other acres of land in St. Lucie County. Benton said this land was anticipated to transition from traditional legacy agricultural or citrus uses to development and will help avoid urban sprawl. "It's an overlay district that's trying to allow for tactful development and new communities that embrace the county's rural character, maintain lands for open space and agricultural activities," said Benton. "It allows for that development very strategically, that considers compatibility and how it's integrated into both the county's need for infrastructure, need for quality of life, jobs, and also connectivity to our interstate and roadway system."

Leah Heinzelmann from Cotleur and Hearing, who is representing the property owners and developer Glassman Holdings LLC, said the development will also include open green space and an over 26-acre park. "The design of it incorporates a lot of open space, really keeping that native buffer along Indrio Road," Heinzelmann said. The rezoning still needs approval from county commissioners in August.

cards.headline: Suspect identified in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher on Essex Drive
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has identified Dale A. Mincey as the suspect in the fatal shooting of 66-year-old Andre Leonard Barnes of Fort Pierce. The shooting occurred Tuesday at a residence in the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle. Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died.

Mincey remains in custody on active felony warrants out of Broward County for dealing in stolen property and false verification to a pawn broker. Barnes was an art teacher for St. Lucie County Schools, and the district released a statement following his death. The homicide investigation remains active, and detectives continue to work with the State Attorney's Office as evidence is reviewed. Additional charges related to this investigation will be determined as the investigation progresses. Deputies said based on the information developed during the investigation, this remains an isolated incident, and there is no threat to the public.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County offers free rip current safety training at public pools this summer
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting three sessions using their new rip current simulation machine to teach proper escape techniques in a controlled environment.
cards.body:
Jennifer Gill, St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation manager, said education is one of the most effective tools to prevent water-related emergencies. The demonstrations allow participants to experience how a rip current works in a safe, controlled environment while learning skills that could save their life or the life of someone they love. The St. Lucie County Parks & Recreation Department is hosting the sessions using their new rip current simulation machine, which creates controlled currents in swimming pools to teach proper escape techniques. According to the National Weather Service, there have been 23 rip current fatalities this year so far in the United States.

The county has scheduled three free demonstrations this summer. On July 19, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Lakewood Park Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. On July 28, a session runs from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Boatwright Pool as part of the Back-to-School Splash Jam event with no registration required on a first-come, first-served basis. On August 16, a session runs from 1 to 4 p.m. at Ravenswood Pool with registration required and limited to 50 participants. Many swimmers make a critical mistake when caught in a rip current by trying to swim directly back to shore, which often leads to dangerous exhaustion. The proper technique is to remain calm, swim parallel to the shoreline until escaping the current, then swim back to shore at an angle.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie City Manager Releases Proposed FY 2026-27 Budget
cards.teaser:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The propo
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Manager Jesus Merejo has released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, outlining nearly $975.3 million in spending across all city funds.

The proposed budget represents a 12.12% increase from the current fiscal year, which the city says is driven by inflation and capital projects. The general fund budget is proposed at about $230.6 million, an 8.48% increase, or roughly $18 million more than FY 2025-26.

The city's taxable value is also expected to rise. According to the budget brief, Port St. Lucie's estimated certified taxable value increased 5.45%, from $25.5 billion in FY 2025-26 to $26.9 billion in FY 2026-27, due to growth and property appreciation.

Under the proposal, the operating millage rate would remain at 4.6607 per $1,000 of taxable value. The total proposed millage rate would remain 4.9750, including the voter-approved Crosstown Parkway debt service millage of 0.3143.

Residents could see some fee changes. The stormwater fee would increase by $6, bringing the residential rate to $195. The solid waste assessment would increase to $482.16 under the city's contract with its solid waste vendor, though qualified residential homeowners would receive a one-time credit of either $364 or $64. The city also proposes a 3.5% increase in the water rate, while the sewer rate would remain unchanged.

The proposed budget also includes long-term infrastructure planning. The city says capital improvement projects over the next five years are projected to cost about $1.069 billion. The largest portion is for utility system upgrades, listed at $672.7 million. Other planned spending includes $51.1 million for Walton & One, Torino & Tradition Regional Parks and O.L. Peacock Park, $34.8 million for facilities maintenance, $24.5 million for street resurfacing and $9.9 million for sidewalk projects.

The budget brief also notes that Port St. Lucie's long-term debt has declined from more than $1.042 billion in FY 2009-10 to a projected $765 million in FY 2026-27, a reduction of 26.58% over 16 years. The proposed budget includes a net increase of seven positions in the Utility Systems Fund, bringing the city to 1,550.25 full-time equivalent positions.

City Council will review the proposed budget during a workshop July 22-23 at the Community Center, located at 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

The workshop will also be televised live on the city's website, Xfinity Channel 20 and Blue Stream Fiber Channel 20.

hero.headline: Second decomposed body found near US-1 in Sebastian, days after first discovery
hero.teaser: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, the second body discovered in the same general area this week.
hero.body: A heavily decomposed body was found in shrubbery along the shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1 in Sebastian Wednesday afternoon, prompting a death investigation by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. A caller reported finding the body shortly after 4 p.m. The body was located on the east side of US 1, across the street from where the body of James Thompson was found Monday. Detectives and Crime Scene Unit personnel are processing the area and working to identify the deceased. Investigators are working to determine whether the two deaths are related or are separate, unconnected incidents occurring in the same general area. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers to remain anonymous.
